hypothesis: At equal area, native vascular plant richness on oceanic islands is much lower than on continental regions, and the gap remains after controlling for climate, latitude and topographic heterogeneity.
pass_criterion: In a regression of log10(native vascular plant species richness) on log10(area), an oceanic-island indicator and the covariates below, the oceanic-island coefficient is negative and its 95% CI excludes 0. The implied ratio at equal area is at most 0.5, meaning the coefficient is at most -0.30 in log10 units. The covariates are absolute latitude, mean annual temperature, annual precipitation and elevational range. The fully adjusted coefficient must also keep at least 50% of the size of the area-only coefficient. Data are restricted to regions with area between 100 and 100,000 km2 so island and mainland areas overlap.
fail_criterion: The adjusted oceanic-island coefficient is greater than -0.30, or its 95% CI includes 0. Alternatively, adding the physical covariates shrinks the coefficient by more than 50% relative to the area-only model, so physical conditions explain the gap. Either result refutes the claim as stated.
interpretation: Darwin's 'species of all kinds' is operationalised as native vascular plant species, the best-inventoried group at global scale. Darwin did not cover other taxa in this test, so the plan covers plants only. 'Oceanic islands' means islands never connected to a continent, i.e. volcanic or atoll islands, using the dataset's island geological-origin classification. 'Continental areas of equal size' means mainland regions or continental-shelf units of comparable area, compared through the species-area relationship. 'Physical conditions' are modern climate, latitude and topographic heterogeneity. 'Far fewer' is set to at least a halving of richness at equal area.

dataset.name: GIFT - Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: Georg-August-Universität Göttingen (Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography group)
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT holds checklist-based native vascular plant species richness for thousands of mainland and island regions worldwide. It records region area, island status and geological origin (oceanic or continental), latitude, climate variables and elevation range. These fields support a species-area comparison between oceanic islands and mainland regions with physical covariates. It is accessible through the GIFT R package and API.
